text.p: Britain's Tate Gallery, famed for its controversial showings of avant garde artists, celebrated its 100th birthday on Monday with landscape painter Prince Charles leading the toasts.
The museum on the banks of the Thames was founded on the fortunes of sugar magnate Sir Henry Tate and was opened in 1897 by King Edward VII when he was Prince of Wales.
Prince Charles enjoyed viewing abstract doodles by Joan Miro, Millais' pre-Raphaelite paintings and an exhibition by local schoolchildren who were told to let their imaginations run riot.
Abstract artist Mondrian is the star of the latest exhibition at the Tate, busy with plans for millennium expansion plans.
The museum started off with just 67 works of art. Its collection has now swelled to 4,000.
